name: Micro servo (SG90, 180°)
description: Hobby servo that turns its horn to an angle from 0 to 180°. Brown wire GND, red 5V, orange signal to any digital pin. In code: #include <Servo.h>, servo.attach(pin), servo.write(angle). It reads 50 Hz pulses: 544 µs = 0°, 1472 µs = 90°, 2400 µs = 180°.

pins.label: V+ (red)
pins.description: Supply 4.8–6 V, red wire. Draws ~10 mA idle, ~250 mA moving, ~650 mA stalled.

pins.label: PWM (orange)
pins.description: Control pulses, orange wire: 50 Hz, 544–2400 µs HIGH.

props.label: Pulse for 0°
props.description: Pulse width that means 0° (Arduino Servo library default 544).

props.label: Pulse for 180°
props.description: Pulse width that means 180° (Servo library default 2400).

props.label: Speed
props.description: Datasheet speed at 4.8 V (SG90: 0.1 s per 60°). Scales with supply voltage.

props.label: Mechanical stop (low)
props.description: Where the horn hits its end stop or the mechanism it drives.

props.label: Angle at power-up
props.description: Where the horn is before the first pulse.

footprint: SG90 micro servo, 23 × 12.2 × 29 mm, 3-wire 0.1 in female connector

bindings.description: Angle the last pulse asked for.
